text: Vietnam marks first legal National E-commerce Day

Known as Online Friday 2026, the week-long event will roll out nationwide across all provinces and cities from December 10 to 16, featuring extensive online promotional programs prioritizing Vietnamese goods and One Commune One Product (OCOP) specialties.

On December 10 and 11, organizers will host a large-scale digital experience space structured around five specialized zones: standard exhibition booths, a main stage for thematic workshops, an E-commerce Clinic advisory area, a livestreaming zone, and an online-to-offline promotional experience hub.
A ceremony celebrating National E-commerce Day will take place at the Hanoi Museum on December 11, paving the way for the nationwide peak online shopping festival on December 12.

Speaking at a press conference in Ho Chi Minh City on November 14, Ms. Le Hoang Oanh, Director of the Vietnam E-commerce and Digital Economy Agency under the Ministry of Industry and Trade, emphasized that holding the first statutory December 12 event lays a solid foundation for the sector's next comprehensive development phase.

She noted that the initiative will expand e-commerce adoption and create fresh opportunities for both citizens and businesses, while calling on media agencies to help amplify the program's message nationwide.

The organizing committee has opened registration via the official portal at onlinefriday.vn, inviting businesses, technology platforms, and merchants to apply for free booth placements, workshops, and advisory sessions before November 30. Beyond serving as a year-end retail stimulus, Online Friday 2026 acts as a resource-connecting lever to help Vietnam sustain its double-digit economic growth momentum.

Despite rapid expansion, the domestic e-commerce market still faces structural disparities between major urban centers and remote areas, large corporations and small household businesses, as well as gaps in generational adoption, digital skills, and legal compliance.
To foster inclusive and sustainable growth, Online Friday 2026 centers on five core pillars.
First, closing the regional gap focuses on extending digital opportunities to all localities and connecting merchants and OCOP products with national and international markets.
Second, addressing the scale gap empowers small and medium-sized enterprises, cooperatives, and household businesses to access digital tools and customer bases on par with major corporations.
Third, bridging the generational gap aims to build a safe, user-friendly online shopping environment for all age groups, from young consumers to seniors and first-time digital shoppers.

Fourth, eliminating the skills gap emphasizes popularizing digital literacy alongside practical skills in store operations, livestreaming, digital advertising, and applying artificial intelligence in business.
Finally, narrowing the legal gap promotes awareness of e-commerce and tax regulations to build a transparent market and safeguard consumer rights.
